messages.subject: [knitLiteral] Chunk hook package for tutorials and examples.
parts:
First push of knitLiteral just went up. It currently only works with markdown
and rmarkdown (v2); .Rnw is next. There are quite a few spots I see it
can be refactored and it will be, but time came to get it out there.

The preview is available at:  http://rpubs.com/Thell/knitLiteralMarkdownPreview

The package is available via github: https://github.com/Thell/knitLiteral

After install, open and knit knitLiteral/examples/Literal-markdown.Rmd

The paths for the style ( and javascript <only needed for v1> ) may need to be
tweaked, but hopefully a way to auto-include those where wanted will be
available soon.

Please give whatever feedback you can.

Thanks, and _have fun_!

Just updated with a "dye" function. Simply include this at the end of your document.

````{r "include-after", echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
# include-after should be the last chunk in the document.
knitLiteral::dye()
````
Updated the rpub example document too.

BTW - you can open and build the example doc that creates the Rpub.
Lcate it on your system using:

system.file( "examples/Literal-markdown.Rmd", package="knitLiteral" )

The markdown to latex does output an extra space on some of the chunks, but that didn't
surprise me as much as things like the blocking of the output and 'collapse' having no effect.

On Saturday, April 12, 2014 5:39:51 PM UTC-5, Rod wrote:
Hi Thell,

I've been working with knitLiteral, and it's going well -- very useful.

But I ran into an unexpected problem with literal code chunks that produce plots and have "echo=FALSE".  (I haven't seen this problem with code chunks that don't produce plots, and I haven't seen it with code chunks that produce plots but have "echo=TRUE".)

I've attached a MWE (and HTML output).

Rod

By indenting the failing chunk 4 spaces the generated markdown is rendered to the document. Doing this shows that a newline is not generated following the closing backticks and before the image tag. The easy fix is to place `eval=FALSE` after literal in the chunk, and then reuse the chunk without echo.

```{r fails, echo=FALSE, literal=TRUE, eval=FALSE}
plot(1:2, 1:2)
```

```{r fails, echo=FALSE}
```

I'll take a look to see where the completing newline is going.

messages.subject: Re: [knitLiteral] Chunk hook package for tutorials and examples.
parts: On Saturday, April 12, 2014 5:39:51 PM UTC-5, Rod wrote:

Hi Thell,

I've been working with knitLiteral, and it's going well -- very useful.

But I ran into an unexpected problem with literal code chunks that produce plots and have "echo=FALSE".  (I haven't seen this problem with code chunks that don't produce plots, and I haven't seen it with code chunks that produce plots but have "echo=TRUE".)

I've attached a MWE (and HTML output).

Rod

Rod,

Taking a look at the knitr plot hook shows that an extra newline is not generated before the image tag is placed in the generated markdown, which makes complete sense as knitr shouldn't be placing extra line endings in documents. This is exactly the type of situation that knitLiteral was made for; displaying what is literally required to get the intended result without breaking the single point of trouble principle. There's an ` opts.label="literal" ` in place for this particular situation, since it is common and should help keep your source file looking clean.

```{r plotting, echo=FALSE, opts.label="literal"}
plot(1:2,1:2)
```

The predefined label templates can be seen using `lapply( knitLiteral:::opt_templates_markdown(), unlist )` until some documentation is made for them, and if you find a particular  set of 'post literal=TRUE' options are being used you can make your own template... just name it 'literal-something'.
